mechanism: Donepezil (cholinesterase inhibitor) enhances acetylcholine activity while oxybutynin (anticholinergic) blocks acetylcholine receptors, creating direct pharmacodynamic opposition that reduces efficacy of both agents.
action: Avoid concurrent use if possible; if combination is necessary, monitor cognitive and urinary symptoms closely and consider alternative anticholinergic agents with less CNS penetration or acetylcholinesterase inhibitor dose adjustment.
